references.text: The Levites were appointed to serve at the tabernacle and take care of it, which corresponds to their role in guarding the Tent of Meeting.
The tribe of Levi was given to Aaron to serve him and carry out the service at the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron and his sons were to oversee the priestly service, and any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
The Levites were given to Aaron and his sons to perform service at the Tent of Meeting.
The priestly service was reserved for Aaron and his sons, and any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
The Israelites were not to come near the Tent of Meeting, so that they would not incur sin and die.
A reminder that no outsider who is not from Aaron's line should come near to burn incense before the Lord.
No outsider was to eat of the holy things, which underscores the prohibition against unauthorized persons approaching sacred matters.
The priestly service was given to Aaron and his sons as a permanent ordinance.
The Levites' task was to stand beside Aaron's sons for the service in the house of the Lord.
